static_traits.name: Xie Xinya
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with friends somewhat strained (frequently talking politics), has a few friends to confide daily problems in
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy received before; no similar psychological problems in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, high cooperation; able to specifically describe Anxiety's impact; tends toward rational analysis and information search on political topics; tone shows Anxiety

basic_info.main_problem: I keep worrying I will vote for the wrong person and they will ruin the country. This worry brings Anxiety and helplessness.
basic_info.core_demands: 'I really just want to no longer feel so overwhelmed and helpless. I hope to make decisions without constantly fearing 'making everything worse'.'
growth_experiences: Political worries and Anxiety began in the last election cycle, feeling overwhelmed facing large amounts of information and opinions; the current political environment intensifies such worries, Anxiety rising as elections approach, triggered almost daily when encountering political news or discussions. Tried researching candidates and policies to ease uncertainty, but Anxiety worsened; followed by poor sleep, eating patterns affected, Tense relationships with friends, and Mild decline in work performance.

core_beliefs: I must make the absolutely correct choice; otherwise the consequences will be disastrous
My decisions will bring serious negative consequences

special_situations.event: Sees political news or discussions on TV or online
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not mastered all information and cannot make a perfect choice, I will choose wrong and cause the country to be destroyed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubles research on candidates and policies, continuously gathers more information to avoid mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will definitely choose wrong; they will ruin the country

special_situations.event: As the election nears and voting day approaches
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot guarantee a completely correct choice, the consequences will be irreversible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly compares candidates, finds it hard to stop thinking, compulsively follows political content
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The closer it gets the more I panic; I may be unable to make the right decision

special_situations.event: When chatting with friends, frequently brings up politics; the other seems bored
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others do not agree or do not participate in discussion, it means I have not fulfilled my responsibility, and I need to work harder to prove I understand enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly raising political topics, seeking others' opinions and approval
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They find me annoying; I must figure it out, otherwise it is my fault

special_situations.event: Extensively researching candidates and policies to ease uncertainty
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not yet mastered all details, I will surely choose the wrong person
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Persistently reads and compares information; deepens research scope and intensity
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I do not know enough yet; the decisions I make now will harm the country

core_conflict.wish: Longs to become a responsible citizen who makes correct choices, affirmed in their judgment and worth
core_conflict.fear: Fears that a wrong choice will lead to catastrophic consequences and being blamed as the cause of 'the country going downhill'
defense_goal: Reducing uncertainty through constant research and rational analysis, avoiding mistakes to ease Anxiety

object_relations.self_representation: An over-responsible bearer, prone to guilt
object_relations.object_representation: Others/media as critics and judges, elections and politics as uncontrollable enormous forces

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor emphasizes 'one person's vote is only part of the bigger picture' and tries to reduce their excessive sense of responsibility
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client may experience it as: if relaxing responsibility, it means not being serious enough or being irresponsible
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizes data, policy details, and logical deduction, avoiding subjective feeling expression; the tone is serious and restrained, with fewer emotion words.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When advised to reduce political news intake and set information boundaries
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worries that reducing information will lead to wrong choices and thus serious consequences
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Opposes the limitation of information on the grounds of 'must fully understand / it is my responsibility'; speech rate on the fast side, nervous tone, continually giving counterexamples.

manifestations: Feeling heavy responsibility and choice Anxiety facing the freedom of voting choice
Views one's individual vote as the key deciding the country's direction, worrying a wrong choice will bring disaster
Feeling uncertain and overwhelmed amid information overload and opinion divergence
outcomes: Sleep impaired and eating patterns disrupted

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Self-blames and highly personalizes election results ('it is all my fault')
Excessively high self-demand to make the 'perfect decision', repeatedly scrutinizes and agonizes

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Viewing voting by the rule 'I must/should get it right'
Treats the external requirement of 'must fully understand the information before voting' as an absolute standard

positive_force: Has a strong sense of responsibility and concern for public affairs
Proactively seeks professional help and is willing to try setting information boundaries
Has information retrieval and rational analysis abilities
Able to notice trigger situations (political news/discussions) and propose initial self-management strategies
negative_force: Catastrophizing, predicting the future and Pronounced black-and-white / all-or-nothing thinking
Personalization and excessive self-blame, increasing the burden
Information overload and compulsive attention, maintaining and escalating Anxiety
Sleep and diet affected lowering emotional tolerance
Tense relationships with friends, further reducing availability of emotional support

target_behavior.behavior: Compulsive information seeking and repeated worry in politically related situations
antecedent: As the election approaches, thinking about voting soon
When political topics come up in social conversation
target_behavior.core_reason: Cognition of catastrophizing and predicting the future, highly personalizing election outcomes and holding black-and-white Demands of 'must get it right', trying to ease uncertainty through information mastery
target_behavior.function: Avoiding Fear of uncertainty and wrong decisions, reducing Anxiety by gaining more information in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Anxiety intensified, sleep and eating patterns impaired, Interpersonal tension, Mild decline in work performance
